textbookText: Nucleic acids are the most essential molecules of life primarily composed of C, O, H, N, and P. They are complex, long-chained and larger than most proteins. These nucleic acids are made up of a few nucleotides. In other words, nucleic acids are the polymers of nucleotides.
Structure of Nucleotide A nucleotide is composed of three components: i. Pentose sugar ii. Nitrogenous bases iii. Phosphoric acid Biology, Grade 11 | 19

Do you know? Friedrich Meischer (1868) isolated nucleic acids from nuclei of pus cells, establishing them as genetic material for all organisms, including viruses. Oswald Avery's (1944) work further supported nucleic acids as carriers of genetic information.

Figure 1.1.20 Three components of nucleotide Do You Know? Nucleosides are the building blocks of nucleotides. For convenience, Nucleoside = Nitrogenous base + Pentose sugar Nucleotide = Nucleoside + Phosphate group
Figure 1.1.20 Structural differences between Nucleoside and nucleotide
i.
Pentose sugar: There are two types of pentose sugars present in two types of nucleic
acids - Ribonucleic acid (RNA) contains ribose sugar and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)
contains deoxyribose sugar.
Biology, Grade 11 | 20
Figure 1.1.21 Structures of deoxyribose and ribose sugars ii. Nitrogen base: They can be categorized into two classes:
1. Purines: There are two rings in their structure (6 + 5 membered). Purines are Adenine (A) and Guanine (G).
2. Pyrimidines: There is one ring in their structure (6 membered). Pyrimidines are Cytosine (C), Thymine (T) and Uracil (U). (Uracil is present only in RNA while Thymine is present only in DNA).
Figure 1.1.22 Structures of purine bases (Adenine and guanine) pyrimidine base (Cytosine, thymine and uracil)
In fact, there exists complementary bases - purine base attaches to specific pyrimidine base, i.e.

• Adenine pairs with Thymine (A = T) by two hydrogen bonds. • Cytosine pairs with Guanine (C≡G) by three hydrogen bonds. iii. Phosphoric acid: It has a phosphate group that connects two nucleotides by a phosphodiester bond.

1. Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) 2. Ribonucleic acid (RNA)

A. Deoxy-Ribonucleic Acid (DNA) DNA is a molecule made of two nucleotide-chains which coil around each other forming a double helix. It present in almost all cells (at nucleus, mitochondria, and plastids) except some viruses. It carries genetic instructions essential for growth, development, functioning and reproduction. A nucleotide has deoxyribose sugar, phosphoric acid, and one of four nitrogenous bases: A, T, G or C.

Figure 1.1.23 DNA Structure (Watson and Crick Model) Characteristics of DNA: − DNA has two parallel chains of polynucleotides running as a right-handed double helix. − The strands are spirally coiled that run in opposite directions (one in 3' - 5' direction and another in 5' - 3'). − They have sugar-phosphate chains outside and purines and pyrimidine bases inside. − These two strands are held together by weak hydrogen bonds between purine (A and G) and pyrimidine bases (T and C). − The distance between strands is 2 nanometer (nm). There are 10 base pairs in a turn (3.4 nm), with a gap of 0.34 nm between pairs. − DNA has 28% adenine, 24% guanine, 20% cytosine, and 28% thymine. − Nucleotides in a helix connect with phospho-diester bonds. Functions of DNA − Being a genetic material, it carries genetic information in the form of a sequence of nitrogenous bases. − DNA copies genetic information to pass it to cells of the next generation.
Biology, Grade 11 | 22

− Crossing over in DNA causes variation in off springs. − Alteration in components of DNA causes mutation, an inheritable genetic change. − Transcription of DNA synthesizes RNAs for different cell functions. − It regulates cellular metabolism through RNA and protein synthesis (Central Dogma).

B. Ribonucleic Acid (RNA) RNA is a single stranded chain of ribonucleotides synthesized in the nucleus but found in the nucleolus, cytoplasm, and on ribosome membranes. Generally, it is single stranded and functions as a hereditary material in some viruses and helps in protein synthesis. Structural Details:

1. RNA is a macromolecule smaller than DNA. 2. It is a single-stranded polynucleotide chain. 3. It is composed of nucleotides linked together by 3'-5' phosphodiester bonds. 4. Each ribonucleotide consists of a ribose sugar, a nitrogen base (Adenine, Guanine,
Cytosine, or Uracil) and a phosphate. Types of RNA:
1. Messenger RNA (mRNA): It is the most abundant type of RNA. It translates genetic information from DNA to ribosomes for protein synthesis.
2. Ribosomal RNA (rRNA): It is a stable RNA linked with ribosomes. 3. Transfer RNA (tRNA): It acts as an adapter, carrying amino acids to the protein
